name: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, severe neonatal type
aliases: Glutaric acidemia type II, neonatal form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (MADD)

criteria.description: Characteristic biochemical profile with elevated multiple acylcarnitines and organic acids in blood and urine
Identification of pathogenic variants in ETFA, ETFB, or ETFDH genes
Severe neonatal onset with metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and congenital anomalies
Ragged red fibers and lipid accumulation in muscle biopsy (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic biochemical abnormalities plus pathogenic variants in ETFA, ETFB, or ETFDH genes with compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical due to rapid progression and high mortality in neonatal period

searchTerms: metabolic acidosis with low blood pH

pathognomonic.notes: Due to impaired fatty acid oxidation
searchTerms: low blood sugar not fixed by glucose
persistent low blood sugar despite glucose

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital anomalies including facial dysmorphism and cystic kidneys
searchTerms: birth defects with facial and kidney cysts
congenital facial abnormalities and kidney cysts
born with facial differences and cystic kidneys

common.notes: Often due to metabolic acidosis and muscle weakness
Due to fatty infiltration and metabolic dysfunction

occasional.notes: Due to secondary urea cycle dysfunction

laboratory: Elevated plasma acylcarnitines of multiple chain lengths
Increased urinary organic acids including glutaric acid and ethylmalonic acid
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
imaging: Cardiomegaly on chest X-ray or echocardiography
Brain MRI may show delayed myelination or cerebral atrophy
other: Muscle biopsy showing lipid accumulation and ragged red fibers
Abnormal electron transport flavoprotein activity assays

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly neurological symptoms without severe metabolic acidosis
Different biochemical profile with elevated glutaric acid but normal acylcarnitine profile
Typically presents later in infancy or childhood

redFlags: Rapidly progressive metabolic acidosis refractory to treatment
Severe hypoglycemia unresponsive to glucose supplementation
Presence of congenital anomalies with metabolic crisis in neonate
references: Roe CR, et al. Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: clinical, biochemical, and molecular aspects. Mol Genet Metab. 2002;77(3):214-223.
Orphanet: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, severe neonatal type. ORPHA:394529.
Fukao T, et al. ETF and ETFDH mutations in multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: molecular and clinical aspects. Hum Mutat. 2014;35(7): 865-874.
